name: Arkansas veterans: county veterans service officers for claims help
organization: County veterans service officers; Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs
description: Free help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits from county veterans service officers. The Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs lists a county veterans service officer for each of the 75 counties; many work only certain days.
next_step: Choose your county for its service officer’s phone and days. The Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs is at 501-683-2382.
constraints: Call before you go; most county officers keep part-time hours, and several share one phone across counties.

name: Choices in Living Resource Center (Arkansas aging and disability resource center)
description: Arkansas’s Aging and Disability Resource Center: information about long-term services and supports for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 866-801-3435, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Arkansas
description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from the State Health Insurance Assistance Program: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare.
next_step: Call 877-839-2675 or use the locator to reach Arkansas’s program. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

source_evidence.title: SHIP Technical Assistance Center: find your local SHIP
source_evidence.scope: National locator and phone 877-839-2675; search excerpt (carried from the starter edition, reviewed November 2, 2026).

name: Arkansas Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Arkansas Department of Human Services, Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, through local ombudsmen at the Area Agencies on Aging.
next_step: Choose your county for its local ombudsman, or call 501-682-1001, the number the state brochure prints for the program. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call the Adult Maltreatment Hotline, 800-482-8049. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

source_evidence.title: National Long-Term Care Ombudsman Resource Center: Arkansas residents’ rights brochure (2026), Contact Your Ombudsman
source_evidence.scope: Program phone 501-682-1001 and website, printed without a label, and every local ombudsman’s counties and phones; read in full.

source_evidence.scope: Program website; read in full. It prints no phone.

name: Free legal help for Arkansas veterans and older adults
description: Free civil legal help for people with low incomes, including housing, benefits and family matters. Legal Aid of Arkansas also runs a statewide fair housing helpline.
next_step: Call the helpline, 800-952-9243 (1-800-9 LAW AID), Monday to Thursday 9 to 11 a.m. and 1 to 3 p.m., and Tuesday evenings 5:15 to 7:15, or apply online any time. Fair housing helpline: 870-338-9834.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type; no criminal cases.
Legal Aid of Arkansas’s application lists 31 counties, so it may refer you to another program; the helpline will say which.

source_evidence.title: Legal Aid of Arkansas: Apply for Legal Aid
source_evidence.scope: Helpline, its hours, the fair housing helpline and the counties on the application; read in full.

name: VA health care systems serving Arkansas
description: Arkansas veterans are served mainly by VA Central Arkansas Health Care (John L. McClellan Memorial Veterans’ Hospital, 4300 West 7th Street, Little Rock; 501-257-1000, toll-free 800-224-8387, with clinics including Conway, El Dorado, Mena, Mountain Home, Pine Bluff, Russellville and Searcy) and the Veterans Health Care System of the Ozarks (1100 North College Avenue, Fayetteville; 479-443-4301, toll-free 800-691-8387).
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic; border counties may be closer to a system in a neighboring state. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

name: Volunteers of America Southeast Louisiana, Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
organization: Volunteers of America Southeast Louisiana, Inc.
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-LA-038): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
